# Psalms of Solomon — Psalm 18 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Vindobonensis) | **Section:** The LORD's Messiah — Blessed Are Those Born in Those Days

---

**18:1** O LORD, your mercy extends over the works of your hands forever;
your kindness covers Israel as a rich gift.

**18:2** Your eyes are upon them and none of them is in want;
your ears are attentive to the hopeful prayer of the poor.

**18:3** Your judgments cover all the earth in mercy;
and your love rests upon the seed of Abraham, the children of Israel.

**18:4** Your chastening is upon us as upon a firstborn, an only son,
to turn back the obedient soul from unintentional sin.

**18:5** May God purify Israel for the day of mercy and blessing,
for the day of election when he brings back his anointed.

**18:6** Blessed are those who shall live in those days,
to behold the good things of the LORD
that he will accomplish for the generation to come;

**18:7** under the rod of discipline of the LORD's anointed,
in the fear of his God,
in the spirit of wisdom and righteousness and strength;

**18:8** to guide every man in the deeds of righteousness by the fear of God,
to establish them all before the LORD;

**18:9** a good generation living in the fear of God,
in the days of his mercy.

**18:10** Great is our God and glorious,
dwelling in the highest heaven;

**18:11** who has set the lights of heaven in their courses
for the reckoning of seasons from year to year,

**18:12** and they have not turned aside from the way he appointed them;
they run their appointed course in the fear of God every day.

**18:13** From the day God created them and forever;
and they have not strayed since the day he created them,
through all the generations of old.

**18:14** They have not deviated from their course except when God commanded them
by the word of his servants.

---

*LOGOS notes: Formal rendering of Ps 18. This psalm closes the Psalms of Solomon collection on a note of cosmic order and messianic hope. The 'anointed' (v.5) links directly to Ps 17's 'LORD Messiah' (17:34).*
